answer: The kiln master weighs every load of limestone and records the hours it burned before the lime is drawn. A nebula load slaked elsewhere fails the register: at the pearl of the kiln the burn must match the master's own hours, and strange lime slakes thin. Faking a burn means hiring a kiln crew, buying stone and paying 12,800, and the ripple line in the burn register is checked at every building site, so lime whose load was never weighed is left in the yard.
